a1.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley states its scale supports continued investment in future technology, including AI and digital tools, positioning it to lead as the future of wealth management takes shape.
items.quote: our scale supports continued investment in future technology, including AI and digital tools.

items.text: Morgan Stanley continues to invest in its technology stack, embracing AI tools to support its infrastructure, business growth and people, positioning to strengthen competitive moats across the integrated firm.
items.quote: We continue to invest across our technology stack, embracing AI tools to support our infrastructure, business growth and people.

items.text: Morgan Stanley's early AI use cases include LeadIQ, an AI-powered lead distribution platform that matches workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitates engagement with financial advisors.
items.quote: LeadIQ, our AI-powered lead distribution platform, focusing on matching workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitating engagement with our financial advisors.

items.text: Morgan Stanley invests in ongoing technology including investments to support its advisors, a build-out of E*TRADE capabilities, and expansion of the workplace channel as engines for future growth.
items.quote: Ongoing investments in our world-class platform, including investments to support our advisors, a build-out of E*TRADE capabilities, and the expansion of our essential workplace channel, serve as an engine for future growth.

items.text: Morgan Stanley uses unique data (from $8.4 trillion of wealth management assets and nearly 21 million households) to equip its own tools that allow financial advisors to tailor advice to help clients achieve their goals.
items.quote: It gives us insights given our size and scale that allow our FAs to tailor advice and equip our own tools to deliver that advice to help clients achieve their goals.

items.text: Morgan Stanley invests in digital tools, digital enhancements and automation to help with the paper backlog associated with lending products.
items.quote: So digital tools, digital enhancements and using automation to be able to help with the paper backlog associated with some of the various lending products more broadly.

items.text: Morgan Stanley is investing in technology centered on building scale and dynamic risk management tools that are paying off in its equities franchise.
items.quote: Investments in technology centered on building scale and dynamic risk management tools are paying off.

items.text: Morgan Stanley cites world-class technology and world-class cyber defense combined with trusted advisers as part of its offering to wealth management and financial adviser clients.
items.quote: this is something we consider to be additive to what we have, which is world-class technology, world-class cyber defense and then the best trusted advisers sitting with the client.

items.text: Morgan Stanley states it has been overweighted to AI from the early days in wealth with work done with OpenAI, and continues to invest in AI.
items.quote: We were, as you know, overweighted to AI from the early days in wealth with some of the work we did with OpenAI.

a1.MS.reason: Multiple passages explicitly state where Morgan Stanley is investing in technology for its advisors, including AI tools, digital tools, data-driven advice tools, LeadIQ, and advisor support investments.

a2.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley is investing to broaden capabilities for financial advisors in: alternatives and privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office and OCIO, and tailored lending.
items.quote: We are using our scale to invest in broadening capabilities for FAs that are difficult for others to replicate: alternatives and privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office and OCIO, and tailored lending.

items.text: Morgan Stanley's scale supports continued investment in future technology including AI and digital tools.
items.quote: our scale supports continued investment in future technology, including AI and digital tools

items.text: Morgan Stanley is developing LeadIQ, an AI-powered lead distribution platform focused on matching workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitating engagement with financial advisors.
items.quote: LeadIQ, our AI-powered lead distribution platform, focusing on matching workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitating engagement with our financial advisors.

items.text: The firm is investing in products like LeadIQ that allow matching individuals with advisers.
items.quote: They're going into products like LeadIQ that will allow us to match individuals with advisers.

items.text: Morgan Stanley is developing co-piloting/'super agents'/corridors to drive efficiency and effectiveness for financial advisors, giving advisors historical context of client interactions.
items.quote: that co-piloting... where they effectively have corridors or super agents that are going to be working to drive, again, efficiency and effectiveness across the portfolio in wealth.

items.text: The firm is developing the DevGen AI tool which enhances developer efficiency by modernizing code.
items.quote: DevGen AI tool, which enhances developer efficiency by modernizing code

items.text: The firm is developing Parable, an interactive tool that quickly analyzes and summarizes data.
items.quote: Parable, an interactive tool that quickly analyzes and summarizes data

items.text: The firm is investing in adjacent digital asset product and announced partnerships with Zero Hash in digital assets.
items.quote: whether it's investing in adjacent digital asset product... we continue to invest, deepening our competitive moats in areas like... digital assets through announced partnerships with Zero Hash.

items.text: Morgan Stanley has invested in E*TRADE Pro, a new tool for the self-directed channel.
items.quote: We've put in new tools like E*TRADE Pro.

items.text: The firm uses unique data from wealth management to allow FAs to tailor advice and equip tools to deliver that advice.
items.quote: It gives us insights given our size and scale that allow our FAs to tailor advice and equip our own tools to deliver that advice to help clients achieve their goals.

items.text: The firm has put digital tools, digital enhancements and automation in place to help with the paper backlog associated with lending products.
items.quote: we've put in a lot of resources towards lending products more broadly. So digital tools, digital enhancements and using automation to be able to help with the paper backlog associated with some of the various lending products more broadly.

items.text: The firm expanded its collaboration with Carta in private markets.
items.quote: deepening our competitive moats in areas like our expanded collaboration with Carta in private markets

a2.MS.reason: Multiple passages state specific tools and capabilities being built or deployed for advisors, satisfying the fact sub-question.

a3.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley's growth plans embed the increasing adoption of AI tools throughout the enterprise and inside its client base, with CEO Ted Pick stating the firm continues to invest in each of its three business segments via human capital and technology.
items.quote: We continue to invest in each of our three business segments: Wealth, Institutional Securities, and Investment Management via human capital and technology. Our growth plans embed the increasing adoption of AI tools throughout the enterprise and inside our client base.

items.text: CEO Ted Pick described AI co-piloting work in wealth management, where Jed Finn under Andy Saperstein is spending time on 'corridors or super agents' to drive efficiency and effectiveness for financial advisers, giving them historical context of past client interactions.
items.quote: you can have the historical context as between the financial adviser and the client where she is well aware of the past interactions... And so that co-piloting, I think, is something that Jed Finn under the leadership of Andy Saperstein is spending a lot of time on where they effectively have corridors or super agents that are going to be working to drive, again, efficiency and effectiveness across the portfolio in wealth.

items.text: CFO Sharon Yeshaya said Morgan Stanley's early AI use cases include LeadIQ, an AI-powered lead distribution platform that matches workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitates engagement with the firm's financial advisors.
items.quote: LeadIQ, our AI-powered lead distribution platform, focusing on matching workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitating engagement with our financial advisors.

items.text: Morgan Stanley said it has ongoing investments in automation and AI and in assessing where it wants its people for the next five to ten years, in the context of a 3% reduction in its XFA (financial advisor) headcount.
items.quote: We have ongoing investments in automation, AI, and assessing where we want our people for the next five, 10 years.

items.text: Morgan Stanley's 10-K states its Wealth Management segment's ability to compete is affected by, among other factors, 'our technology supporting evolving client needs, including generative artificial intelligence and tokenization.'
items.quote: our ability to effectively compete against many of our competitors across different channels (i.e., advisor led, workplace and digital direct) is affected by multiple factors including our brand and reputation, the breadth, depth and pricing of our product offerings and our technology supporting evolving client needs, including generative artificial intelligence and tokenization.

a3.MS.reason: Multiple passages describe Morgan Stanley's AI and automation initiatives directed at financial advisors, including LeadIQ, co-piloting work in wealth, and investment in AI tools throughout the enterprise.

a4.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley's CEO describes AI as an existentially important top priority, with the firm overweighted to AI in wealth from its early work with OpenAI.
items.quote: We were, as you know, overweighted to AI from the early days in wealth with some of the work we did with OpenAI... There is just no question that this is existentially important that we are viewed as a trusted adviser in the middle of the ecosystem... And for us to be part of the content and the thinking and the evolution of this is absolutely the top priority for the firm as the adviser

items.text: Morgan Stanley identifies AI use cases including DevGen AI, Parable, and LeadIQ, which focuses on matching workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitating engagement with financial advisors.
items.quote: These include the DevGen AI tool, which enhances developer efficiency by modernizing code, Parable, an interactive tool that quickly analyzes and summarizes data, and LeadIQ, our AI-powered lead distribution platform, focusing on matching workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitating engagement with our financial advisors.

items.text: Morgan Stanley describes technology as investing in broadening capabilities for financial advisors that are difficult for others to replicate: alternatives and privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office and OCIO, and tailored lending.
items.quote: We are using our scale to invest in broadening capabilities for FAs that are difficult for others to replicate: alternatives and privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office and OCIO, and tailored lending.

items.text: Morgan Stanley continues to invest in future technology including AI and digital tools, with scale supporting continued investment.
items.quote: our scale supports continued investment in future technology, including AI and digital tools.

items.text: Morgan Stanley describes technology as a differentiator in its favor, built against the platform of self-directed, workplace and financial advisor channels.
items.quote: against that platform, we have built a number of advantages that not only allow us to preserve our moat, but actually make technology a differentiator in our favor.

items.text: Morgan Stanley's CEO describes technology as being able to help financial advisors do a lot of the early work on clients' complex financial decisions, while remaining a people business.
items.quote: if the technology is world-class, folks want to make decisions with their financial advisers based on the complexity and singularity of their own financial needs... that is something that technology can help do a lot of the early work.

items.text: Morgan Stanley states it is investing in technology, distribution, and product innovation to serve its global client base across its franchise.
items.quote: our ongoing investments in technology, distribution, and product innovation position our diversified franchise to better serve our global client base.

a4.MS.reason: Multiple passages describe Morgan Stanley's technology priorities for the advisor business, including AI, digital tools, and capabilities for financial advisors.

claims.text: On the 3Q26 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2026), Morgan Stanley states its scale supports continued investment in future technology, including AI and digital tools, positioning it to lead as the future of wealth management takes shape.

On the 3Q26 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2026), Morgan Stanley states it continues to invest in its technology stack, embracing AI tools to support its infrastructure, business growth and people, positioning to strengthen competitive moats across the integrated firm.

On the 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), Morgan Stanley states, in Wealth Management, that its early AI use cases include LeadIQ, an AI-powered lead distribution platform that matches workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitates engagement with financial advisors.

On the 2Q25 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2025), Morgan Stanley states, in Wealth Management, that it invests in ongoing technology including investments to support its advisors, a build-out of E*TRADE capabilities, and expansion of the workplace channel as engines for future growth.

On the 3Q26 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2026), Morgan Stanley states, in Wealth Management, that it uses unique data (from $8.4 trillion of wealth management assets and nearly 21 million households) to equip its own tools that allow financial advisors to tailor advice to help clients achieve their goals.

On the 1Q26 earnings call (period ended March 31, 2026), Morgan Stanley states, in Wealth Management, that it invests in digital tools, digital enhancements and automation to help with the paper backlog associated with lending products.

On the 2Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), Morgan Stanley states, in its Institutional Securities equities franchise, that it is investing in technology centered on building scale and dynamic risk management tools that are paying off.

On the 1Q26 earnings call (period ended March 31, 2026), Morgan Stanley cites world-class technology and world-class cyber defense combined with trusted advisers as part of its offering to wealth management and financial adviser clients.

On the 3Q26 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2026), Morgan Stanley states, in Wealth Management, that it has been overweighted to AI from the early days in wealth with work done with OpenAI, and continues to invest in AI.

On the 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), Morgan Stanley states it is developing LeadIQ, an AI-powered lead distribution platform focused on matching workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitating engagement with financial advisors.
On the 2Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), Morgan Stanley states the firm is investing in products like LeadIQ that allow matching individuals with advisers.
On the 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), Morgan Stanley states the firm is developing the DevGen AI tool which enhances developer efficiency by modernizing code.
On the 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), Morgan Stanley states the firm is developing Parable, an interactive tool that quickly analyzes and summarizes data.

On the 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), Morgan Stanley states, in Wealth Management, that the firm is investing in adjacent digital asset product and announced partnerships with Zero Hash in digital assets.
On the 2Q25 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2025), Morgan Stanley states, for the self-directed channel / E*TRADE, that it has invested in new tools like E*TRADE Pro.

On the 1Q26 earnings call (period ended March 31, 2026), Morgan Stanley states the firm has put digital tools, digital enhancements and automation in place to help with the paper backlog associated with lending products.
On the 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), Morgan Stanley states the firm expanded its collaboration with Carta in private markets.

On the 1Q26 earnings call (period ended March 31, 2026), CEO Ted Pick described, in Wealth Management, AI co-piloting work where Jed Finn under Andy Saperstein is spending time on corridors or super agents to drive efficiency and effectiveness for financial advisers, giving them historical context of past client interactions. Why it might matter: the CEO described the co-piloting as something that over time becomes a productivity phenomenon, with the efficiency and effectiveness being compelling.

Morgan Stanley's 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states its Wealth Management segment's ability to compete is affected by, among other factors, its technology supporting evolving client needs, including generative artificial intelligence and tokenization. Why it might matter: the 10-K states the firm's ability to compete across advisor-led, workplace and digital direct channels is affected by multiple factors including brand and reputation and the breadth, depth and pricing of its product offerings.

On the 4Q25 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2025), Morgan Stanley states its growth plans embed the increasing adoption of AI tools throughout the enterprise and inside its client base, with CEO Ted Pick stating the firm continues to invest in each of its three business segments via human capital and technology. Why it might matter: the firm said its confidence continues to increase each quarter in the potential for both the efficiency and the effectiveness of AI-related technologies across the business units and infrastructure.

On the 1Q25 earnings call (period ended March 31, 2025), Morgan Stanley said it has ongoing investments in automation and AI and in assessing where it wants its people for the next five to ten years, in the context of a 3% reduction in its XFA (financial advisor) headcount. Why it might matter: the firm said it will be reviewing the overall workforce regularly, given some uncertainty in the environment.

On the 3Q26 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2026), Morgan Stanley's CEO describes, in Wealth Management, AI as an existentially important top priority, with the firm overweighted to AI in wealth from its early work with OpenAI.

On the 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), Morgan Stanley identifies, in Wealth Management, AI use cases including DevGen AI, Parable, and LeadIQ, which focuses on matching workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitating engagement with financial advisors.

On the 4Q25 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2025), Morgan Stanley describes, in Wealth Management, technology as investing in broadening capabilities for financial advisors that are difficult for others to replicate: alternatives and privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office and OCIO, and tailored lending.

On the 3Q26 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2026), Morgan Stanley states, in Wealth Management, that it continues to invest in future technology including AI and digital tools, with scale supporting continued investment.

On the 3Q26 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2026), Morgan Stanley describes, in Wealth Management, technology as a differentiator in its favor, built against the platform of self-directed, workplace and financial advisor channels.

On the 3Q26 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2026), Morgan Stanley's CEO describes, in Wealth Management, technology as being able to help financial advisors do a lot of the early work on clients' complex financial decisions, while remaining a people business.

On the 2Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), Morgan Stanley states, in Investment Management, that it is investing in technology, distribution, and product innovation to serve its global client base across its franchise.

claims.text: Merrill is the most explicit of the five in naming the mass-affluent client segment. The comparison is valid on this evidence because Merrill is the only firm whose cited materials define a 'Mass Affluent' tier by name: its investor-day deck (published 2025-11-05) labels 'Mass Affluent ($500K - $1MM)' within a 'Wealth Continuum.' By contrast, Morgan Stanley's 10-K (period 2025-12-31) describes its Wealth Management clients as 'high and ultra-high net worth individuals' and references 'mass-affluent' only as a third-party Cerulli survey category, not its own segmentation; Schwab's transcripts use 'affluent' and 'higher net worth' without defining a 'mass-affluent' tier; Edward Jones' 10-K names 'High Net Worth' but not mass-affluent; and Raymond James (trade press) uses 'high-net-worth' (defined as at least $5 million in investable assets) and 'ultra-high-net-worth,' not mass-affluent. The firms are not all on the same basis, so only Merrill can be said to explicitly name and define a mass-affluent segment.

items.text: Edward Jones is pursuing a new digital platform focused on attracting and retaining Next Generation investors, indicating a move toward digital/self-directed-style offerings for younger investors.
items.quote: and a new digital platform, focused on attracting and retaining Next Generation investors.

items.text: Edward Jones cites changing client preferences and values, changing client demographics, and generational wealth transfer as factors that may adversely impact its ability to compete and adapt its business model, including expanded product offerings and technology needs.
items.quote: The Partnership's continued ability to compete and adapt its business model may be adversely impacted by the evolving financial services industry and generational wealth transfer, including changing client expectations for expanded product offerings and technology needs, and changing client demographics, preferences and values.

items.text: Edward Jones notes the financial services industry is evolving technologically, with an increasing number of firms providing enhanced digital experiences and lower cost computer-based robo-advice, and competition from firms offering discount services and fintech companies with internet- and mobile-based platforms.
items.quote: an increasing number of firms of all sizes providing enhanced digital experiences for clients, including the utilization of artificial intelligence technologies and lower cost, computer-based "robo-advice."

items.text: In its 10-K risk factors, Edward Jones identifies generational wealth transfer and changing client demographics, preferences and values as strategic risks it seeks to address through initiatives to deliver enhanced value and impact.
items.quote: changing client demographics, preferences and values, technology, artificial intelligence, and regulatory changes, through its initiatives to deliver enhanced value and impact for millions of current and potential clients, colleagues and communities.

items.quote: Edward Jones announced that they have taken a minority stake in the personal finance app Quicken, with an explicit intention that the investment is a step towards integrating Quicken's personal financial management capabilities more directly into Edward Jones as a way to support their value proposition and advisor conversations with clients.

items.text: Edward Jones offers Financial Planning Services, where clients receive a more personalized experience with additional planning capabilities.

items.text: Edward Jones's Digital and Data division supports investment in technology infrastructure and digital initiatives to provide new tools for branch teams and create operational efficiencies; branch teams leverage new tools for deeper discovery conversations and more comprehensive advice and planning.
items.quote: The Partnership's Digital and Data division supports the significant investment in technology infrastructure and digital initiatives to provide new tools for branch teams to better serve clients... claims.text: Schwab: On its 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), Schwab stated that one-third of retail households who created a financial plan within the last two years are under the age of 40, showing younger investors are engaged in building wealth over the long term.

Schwab: On its 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), Schwab stated that younger traders turn to Schwab because they recognize the potential that trading has in helping build wealth over time, and for the platforms, tools, education, coaching, expertise, and service to help them succeed.

Schwab: On its 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), Schwab stated that younger investors are attracted through its trading platform thinkorswim, digital capabilities, support, service, and education including 35 hours a week of live content on how to trade and invest.

Schwab: On its 2Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), Schwab stated that younger investors are engaged with trading, with growth in comfort with options trading as a way to add income or hedge portfolios, and use of AI for research and trading.
Schwab: On its 2Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), Schwab stated that the removal of commissions brought more people with less money into the market, including young investors.
Schwab: On its 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), Schwab stated that crypto will certainly appeal to young investors.

Schwab: In its 3Q26 investor deck (period ended September 30, 2026), Schwab stated that its client engagement preferences span digital-first to relationship-led, and its investing styles span self-directed to advised.

Schwab: In its 2026 investor day deck (published May 14, 2026), Schwab stated that 42% of thinkorswim users are Millennial or Gen Z, showing younger investors' product use and engagement with the trading platform.
Schwab: On its 2Q25 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2025), Schwab stated that young investors want to think about how to pay off their college debt and how to buy a house.

Industry research: A Bank of America Private Bank study (published June 17, 2026) reports that 47% of young investors use AI to research companies or markets, 87% are comfortable with advisors using AI to help manage portfolios, and 65% still prefer to receive investment advice from a human advisor.

Industry research: A Bank of America Private Bank study (published June 17, 2026) reports that younger investors (Gen Z/Millennials) allocate 32 percent of their portfolios to stocks, versus 58 percent for older investors (Gen X/Baby Boomers).

Industry research: A Bank of America Private Bank study (published June 18, 2024) reports that Millennials and Gen Z allocate three times more of their investment portfolios to alternative investments than older generations, looking beyond traditional stock and bond markets, driving demand for investment real estate, private equity, digital assets, and gold.

Industry research: A Bank of America Private Bank study (published June 18, 2024) reports that for investors aged 21-43, the greatest opportunities for growth are real estate investments (31%), crypto/digital assets (28%), private equity (26%), personal company/brand (24%), direct investment into companies (22%), and companies focused on positive impact (21%).

Industry research: A Bank of America Private Bank study (published June 17, 2026) reports that 42% of younger respondents own art; among those who do not, 75% are interested in owning art, and 94% own collectables.

Schwab: On its 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), Schwab stated that younger investors (Gen Z) learn about finances primarily through social media and family, and Schwab is meeting them in the channels where they turn for information about investing.

Schwab: On its 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), Schwab stated that their top online resource is YouTube, and Schwab is the number one financial services firm on YouTube by followers.

Edward Jones: The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states that Edward Jones is pursuing a new digital platform focused on attracting and retaining Next Generation investors, indicating a move toward digital/self-directed-style offerings for younger investors.

Edward Jones: The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states that Edward Jones cites changing client preferences and values, changing client demographics, and generational wealth transfer as factors that may adversely impact its ability to compete and adapt its business model, including expanded product offerings and technology needs.

Edward Jones: The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states that Edward Jones notes the financial services industry is evolving technologically, with an increasing number of firms providing enhanced digital experiences and lower cost computer-based robo-advice, and competition from firms offering discount services and fintech companies with internet- and mobile-based platforms.

Edward Jones: The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025), in its risk factors, identifies generational wealth transfer and changing client demographics, preferences and values as strategic risks it seeks to address through initiatives to deliver enhanced value and impact.

Industry research: A Cerulli report (published October 29, 2025) finds that younger investors prefer to retain a greater degree of control of at least part of their investing lives, whereas older investors tend to be more advisor-reliant.

Schwab: In its 2026 investor day deck (published May 14, 2026), Schwab reports new-to-firm retail household growth of 1.0M in 2023, 1.1M in 2024, and 1.2M in 2025, a +10% CAGR, driven in part by strong growth and winning with young investors.
Schwab: On its 3Q26 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2026), Schwab states approximately 70% of new-to-firm retail households are Gen Z and millennials.

Schwab: On its 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), Schwab stated that industry research shows Gen Z is 45% more likely to start investing by age 21 compared to Millennials, and nearly one-third of new-to-firm retail households at Schwab are Gen Zers, investors between the ages of 13 and 28.

Schwab: On its 4Q25 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2025), Schwab states Gen Z investors comprise nearly a third of new retail client accounts opened in 2025, and nearly 60% are under the age of 40.

Schwab: In its 2026 investor day deck (published May 14, 2026), Schwab reports 61% of new clients are Gen Z & Millennial investors, and +14% new-to-firm retail households and +25% new-to-firm retail NNA growth from 2024 to 2025.

Schwab: On its 2Q25 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2025), Schwab reports one in six new-to-firm retail households are under age 24, more than 30% of new-to-firm clients are under age 30, and nearly 60% are under age 40.
Schwab: On its 4Q24 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2024), Schwab reports 33% of new-to-firm retail households are under age 30, and more than 50% are under age 40.

Schwab: On its 4Q25 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2025), Schwab states its average client age has fallen by about 10 years in the last decade and is now in the 40s, and a third of new-to-firm clients last year were Gen Z investors.
Schwab: In its 3Q26 investor deck (period ended September 30, 2026), Schwab reports ~70% of new-to-firm retail households are Gen Z & Millennials.
Schwab: In its 2026 investor day deck (published May 14, 2026), Schwab reports +60% of new-to-firm retail households are under age 40.

Edward Jones: A trade report (published August 18, 2026) states Edward Jones announced it has taken a minority stake in the personal finance app Quicken, intending the investment as a step toward integrating Quicken's personal financial management capabilities more directly into Edward Jones to support its value proposition and advisor conversations with clients.

Edward Jones: The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states that Edward Jones offers Financial Planning Services, where clients receive a more personalized experience with additional planning capabilities.

Edward Jones: The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states that Edward Jones targets new clients through the High Net Worth initiative and a new digital platform focused on Next Generation investors, and through Workplace which connects business owners and employees with financial solutions.

Edward Jones: A trade report (published September 30, 2026) states Edward Jones is partnering with Aboon and Retirement Plan Advisory Group to develop an end-to-end retirement plan management tool, leveraging an AI-native platform.

Edward Jones: The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states that Edward Jones's Digital and Data division supports investment in technology infrastructure and digital initiatives to provide new tools for branch teams and create operational efficiencies; branch teams leverage new tools for deeper discovery conversations and more comprehensive advice and planning.

Edward Jones: The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states that Edward Jones notes changing client expectations for expanded product offerings and technology needs and changing client demographics, preferences and values tied to generational wealth transfer as factors affecting its ability to compete.

Edward Jones: The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states that Edward Jones aspires to anticipate clients' needs with the right offering at the right time, now and for generations to come, and to attract and serve new client segments.

Edward Jones: The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states that Edward Jones's strategic ambition is to help tens of millions of investors achieve financial fulfillment through personalized, comprehensive planning and trusted advice, which includes continuing to invest in technology to scale financial planning.

Edward Jones: The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states that Edward Jones's continued ability to compete and adapt may be adversely impacted by changing client demographics, preferences and values, including generational wealth transfer and changing client expectations for technology.

Schwab: On its 2Q25 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2025), Schwab states it does not report how its strategy or priorities apply to Edward Jones, because Edward Jones is a different firm from Schwab; the passages instead describe Schwab's own strategy for attracting and serving younger investors.

Schwab: In its 2026 investor day deck (published May 14, 2026), Schwab states it serves younger investors through the Schwab Starter Kit and Schwab Teen Investor Account, and offers no/low commissions.

Schwab: On its 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), Schwab states it meets younger investors in the channels where they turn for information about investing, noting they learn about finances primarily through social media and family, and that their top online resource is YouTube, where Schwab is the number one financial services firm by followers.

Schwab: In its 2026 investor day deck (published May 14, 2026), Schwab states it offers the thinkorswim trading platform and digital capabilities, with 42% of thinkorswim users being Millennial or Gen Z.

Schwab: On its 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), Schwab states it provides 35 hours a week of live content, plus education, coaching, service and expertise to help young investors learn to trade and invest.

Schwab: On its 2Q25 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2025), Schwab states it offers in-person experiences in over 400 locations and has 16,000 advisors in every community that young investors can walk in and talk to, positioned as the best place for young investors considering things like paying off college debt or buying a house.

Schwab: On its 2Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026) and 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), Schwab states its strategy for younger investors includes supporting growth in young investors through the removal of commissions and anticipation that crypto will be additive and appeal to young investors.

The comparison of Edward Jones's disclosures and initiatives for younger investors to those of competitors cannot be made on this evidence. Edward Jones's disclosures and initiatives are documented — a new digital platform for attracting and retaining Next Generation investors, a minority stake in Quicken to support its value proposition and advisor conversations, targeting of new clients through High Net Worth and Workplace, and strategic ambitions to anticipate clients' needs and attract and serve new client segments while addressing generational wealth transfer — but equivalent disclosures and initiatives for younger investors from the competitor firms (Morgan Stanley, Charles Schwab, Merrill, Raymond James Financial) were not found in the documents searched, so there is no like-for-like basis for comparison.

The evidence above only provides objective context for the strategic question asked. Whether or how Edward Jones should act is a judgment for the strategy team to make, beyond the scope of this evidence engine.

a3.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley's strategic client acquisition model comprises three channels - financial advisors, Workplace, and E*TRADE - that together funnel client relationships and assets toward advisor-led, fee-based relationships as clients' wealth grows.
items.quote: Our financial advisors, Workplace, and E*TRADE, each a category leader, which taken together comprise our strategic client acquisition model.

items.text: Morgan Stanley states it retains 99% of its clients and that 60% of advisor-led assets are associated with clients who have an average duration of 20 years.
items.quote: 60% of advisor-led assets are associated with clients who have an average duration of 20 years. We retain 99% of our clients, reflecting their enduring trust in Morgan Stanley.

items.text: Morgan Stanley's 'funnel' concept retains workplace assets as they vest and migrates them over time into advisor-led relationships, with over $1 trillion of total assets in the advisor-led strategy contributed by that migration.
items.quote: The first is we retain those assets... we are seeing channel migration, and that's with technology and investment, where those Workplace assets are now actually seeking advice and that migration is something that has helped to contribute to over $1 trillion of total assets in our adviser-led strategy.

items.text: Since 2020, Morgan Stanley generated over $400 billion of new advisor-led assets from relationships originating in Workplace or E*TRADE; inclusive of Workplace assets prior to the E*TRADE acquisition, advisor-led assets sourced from Workplace and E*TRADE exceed $1.2 trillion, roughly 20% of advisor-led assets.
items.quote: Since 2020, we have generated over $400 billion of new adviser-led assets from relationships that originated from either Workplace or E*TRADE... the total value of adviser-led assets sourced from Workplace and E*TRADE exceeds $1.2 trillion.

items.text: Morgan Stanley is using its scale to invest in broadening advisor capabilities around alternatives and privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office and OCIO, and tailored lending to help retain assets and relationships for the next generation.
items.quote: We are using our scale to invest in broadening capabilities for FAs that are difficult for others to replicate: alternatives and privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office and OCIO, and tailored lending.

items.text: Morgan Stanley's deck shows how it serves clients across their lifecycle and wealth transfer: Founders Wealth Strategies, Family Office Solutions, Trust & Estate Planning, and financial wellness and employee benefits for the next generation.
items.quote: Financial Wellness and Employee Benefits / Founders Wealth Strategies / Full-Service Wealth Advice and Asset Allocation / Family Office Solutions, Trust & Estate Planning

items.text: Morgan Stanley retains assets that vest in its Workplace channel and migrates them into advisor-led relationships, which the firm describes as its client acquisition 'funnel' and retention strategy.
items.quote: we saw unvested assets vest. And what we saw in Workplace this quarter is greater retention of the assets that vested... Then over time... we are seeing channel migration... where those Workplace assets are now actually seeking advice

items.text: Morgan Stanley invests in referral models and products like LeadIQ to match individuals with advisers, with the stated goal of being each client's principal financial adviser and migrating flows into fee-based advice over the long term.
items.quote: They're going into creating our referral models. They're going into products like LeadIQ that will allow us to match individuals with advisers. And our goal is to be their principal financial adviser... that migration of those flows into fee-based and path to advice.

items.text: As lockups and funds make distributions, Morgan Stanley sees further opportunities to retain assets and attach clients to E*TRADE, workplace, and ultimately fee-based advisory flows.
items.quote: as lockups and funds make distributions, there are further opportunities to retain assets... fee-based flows that make their way to the advisers

items.text: Morgan Stanley sees a great opportunity with 'assets held away' - individuals who have just stepped into wealth and begin to consolidate assets, understanding the value of a fulsome advice-based relationship.
items.quote: These individuals have just stepped into wealth. They begin to consolidate assets and understand the value of a fulsome advice-based relationship.

items.text: Morgan Stanley describes how its integrated firm serves clients through growth cycles including generational wealth transfer, from founders/employees to preserve wealth and unlock liquidity.
items.quote: Corporates / Founders / Employees / Early Stage / Public Company / Invest for the Future / Preserve Wealth / Unlock Liquidity

a3.MS.reason: The passages describe Morgan Stanley's multichannel funnel, advisor retention and capability investments, and lifecycle services including trust and estate planning and family office solutions, which constitute the firm's preparation to retain assets as wealth transfers to next-generation heirs.

a4.MS.label: different_quantity

items.text: The firm increased the cash component of advisor compensation in 2026 and reduced the amount of deferred compensation as a proportion of total compensation for Wealth Management advisors, changes described as supporting investment into financial advisors and simplifying the compensation program.
items.quote: we will also increase the cash component of our advisor compensation. We are making these changes to reduce the accounting-driven volatility in revenues and earnings. ... these changes support our overall investment into our financial advisors and will help simplify our compensation program.

items.text: In the first quarter of 2026 the Firm reduced the amount of deferred compensation as a proportion of total compensation for Wealth Management advisors.
items.quote: in the first quarter of 2026, the Firm reduced the amount of deferred compensation as a proportion of total compensation for Wealth Management advisors.

items.text: Morgan Stanley is increasing a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027 and is not introducing retention bonuses as part of its 2027 advisor pay plan, adhering to a more traditional approach, unlike competitors.
items.quote: Morgan Stanley and Merrill Lynch are not introducing retention bonuses as part of their 2027 pay plans for advisors, adhering to a more traditional approach. As it has in the past, Morgan Stanley is increasing a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027, meaning advisors have to generate that much more revenue to see the same pay next year.

items.text: Morgan Stanley uses deferred compensation as a retention tool, taking a small amount of an advisor's gross revenue as deferred compensation and requiring advisors to stay for years to vest -- described as 'golden handcuffs.'
items.quote: Giants like Morgan Stanley for years have taken a small amount of an advisor's gross revenue, called it deferred compensation, and required advisors to stay for years in order to vest. If a financial advisor leaves a firm with a deferred compensation plan, he or she forfeits that compensation, which is also known on Wall Street as golden handcuffs.

a4.MS.differs_because: The sub-question asks about how firms prepare for advisor succession and retirement given an aging advisor force and clients. The passages describe advisor compensation/retention mechanisms (deferred compensation, pay thresholds, cash compensation changes) rather than a succession or retirement-planning program for advisors or an aging advisor force figure.
a4.MS.reason: No passage states a specific advisor succession/retirement preparation program or aging-advisor-force data; only related advisor compensation and retention measures are discussed.

a5.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley's Wealth Management supports clients through three channels—Advisor-Led, Self-Directed, and Workplace—and includes financial advisor-led brokerage, investment advisory, custody, cash management, administrative services, self-directed brokerage, financial and wealth planning, workplace services including stock plan administration, securities-based lending, residential and commercial real estate loans, banking, and retirement plan services.
items.quote: Wealth Management supports clients through three channels: Advisor-Led, Self-Directed and Workplace. Wealth Management includes: financial advisor-led brokerage, investment advisory, custody, cash management, and administrative services; self-directed brokerage services; financial and wealth planning services; workplace services, including stock plan administration; securities-based lending, residential and commercial real estate loans and other lending products; banking; and retirement plan services.

items.text: Morgan Stanley describes its integrated firm's capabilities through clients' growth cycles, offering Founders Wealth Strategies at early stage, full-service wealth advice and asset allocation, family office solutions and trust & estate planning for preserving wealth, and private shares trading and lending and IPO execution to unlock liquidity.
items.quote: Founders / Employees ... Early Stage ... Invest for the Future ... Financial Wellness and Employee Benefits ... Founders Wealth Strategies ... Preserve Wealth ... Full-Service Wealth Advice and Asset Allocation ... Family Office Solutions, Trust & Estate Planning ... Unlock Liquidity ... Private Shares Trading & Lending ... IPO Execution and Support Services

items.text: Morgan Stanley states it invests to broaden financial advisor capabilities including alternatives and privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office and OCIO, and tailored lending.
items.quote: We are using our scale to invest in broadening capabilities for FAs that are difficult for others to replicate: alternatives and privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office and OCIO, and tailored lending.

items.text: Morgan Stanley expanded its collaboration with Carta in private markets and in digital assets through announced partnerships with Zero Hash to service clients with unique capabilities.
items.quote: In the third quarter, we continue to invest, deepening our competitive moats in areas like our expanded collaboration with Carta in private markets and in digital assets through announced partnerships with Zero Hash.

items.text: Morgan Stanley's Parametric platform offers custom investment solutions and separately managed accounts, and the firm highlights retail-oriented distribution offerings flowing through the Wealth Management relationship.
items.quote: Our industry-leading Parametric platform, Inclusive of Overlay, has grown to $575 billion... the relationship with Wealth Management, continues to benefit the Investment Management platform with the enhancement of retail-oriented distribution offerings and additional product capabilities.

items.text: Morgan Stanley offers evergreen products and products that allow for lower denomination size to make private alternatives more accessible to retail clients.
items.quote: We're offering new products to our clients, such as evergreen products and products that allow for lower denomination size.

items.text: Morgan Stanley's E*TRADE self-directed platform and workplace channel serve as the top-of-funnel client acquisition with financial education and referral model beginning at the financial education spot, feeding into advice-based relationships.
items.quote: we're working on that referral model. And that's something that can begin as early as the financial education spot, and it can also begin -- like I said, we have examples with 401(k)s and new 401(k) assets... I'm really giving people that ability to better understand where they could use advice.

items.text: Morgan Stanley acquired E*TRADE and expanded workplace offering; since 2020 it generated over $400 billion of new adviser-led assets from relationships that originated from Workplace or E*TRADE.
items.quote: Since 2020, we have generated over $400 billion of new adviser-led assets from relationships that originated from either Workplace or E*TRADE.

items.text: Morgan Stanley provides family office solutions and OCIO, and does work servicing founders and family offices as part of its wealth coverage.
items.quote: We've done a lot of work on trying to service founders, on trying to service family offices.

a5.MS.reason: The passages describe specific products, services, and platforms (channels, alternatives, Parametric, Carta/Zero Hash partnerships, family office solutions, E*TRADE/workplace funnel) that Morgan Stanley offers to attract and serve next-generation clients.

a6.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley's integrated firm strategy positions it to support clients throughout an entire life cycle, engaging entire families and facilitating multi-generational wealth planning, including solutions for founders and employees, family office solutions, and trust & estate planning.
items.quote: We have scaled capabilities and a business mix that can support our clients throughout an entire life cycle... Our Morgan Stanley at Work business, with its exclusive partnership with Carta, positions us as an early trusted advisor to over 50,000 private companies.

items.text: Morgan Stanley offers a range of capabilities to serve clients across growth cycles, including Founders Wealth Strategies, Family Office Solutions, Trust & Estate Planning, and Full-Service Wealth Advice and Asset Allocation, which facilitate multi-generational wealth planning.
items.quote: Financial Wellness and Employee Benefits / Founders Wealth Strategies / Full-Service Wealth Advice and Asset Allocation / Family Office Solutions, Trust & Estate Planning

items.text: Morgan Stanley highlights family office and OCIO, along with tailored lending, among capabilities being broadened for financial advisors, which supports engaging ultra-high net worth families.
items.quote: We are using our scale to invest in broadening capabilities for FAs that are difficult for others to replicate: alternatives and privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office and OCIO, and tailored lending.

items.text: Morgan Stanley provides ultra-high net worth family office infrastructure solutions, which facilitate engaging entire families and multi-generational wealth planning.
items.quote: then importantly, for ultra-high net worth family office infrastructure solutions.

items.text: Morgan Stanley has done work on servicing founders and family offices, deepening Wealth Management coverage of individuals across their journey.
items.quote: We've done a lot of work on trying to service founders, on trying to service family offices. There are all different places when you can think about how we've grown our Wealth Management business in terms of the types of coverage we give to the individuals.

items.text: Morgan Stanley's integrated firm proposition is that a trusted advisor to a founder can be connected to a wealth manager, who can then work with the investment banker, facilitating engagement across the founder's family and business wealth.
items.quote: you may be trusted advisor to a founder, and that founder may have a relationship with a wealth manager, and that wealth manager then can work with the investment banker.

a6.MS.reason: Multiple passages describe Morgan Stanley's engagement of families and multi-generational wealth planning through family office solutions, trust & estate planning, founder wealth strategies, and integrated-firm lifecycle coverage.

a7.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley articulated a strategy to 'raise, manage, and allocate capital' for clients and described its four pillars of the integrated firm (strategy, culture, financial strength, growth) as central to capturing client share.
items.quote: Strategy is about consistently serving our clients in raising, managing, and allocating capital... The investment thesis for Morgan Stanley rests on our ability to deliver the integrated firm supported by these four pillars.

items.text: Chairman and CEO Ted Pick stated the firm is focused on the 'core strategy of raise, manage, and allocate capital' and on nurturing existing businesses, with acquisitions evaluated only if they fit the strategy and offer incremental operating leverage.
items.quote: we're really focused on what is in front of us in our operating and management committee and leadership meetings... The nurturing of what we have in the core strategy of raise, manage, and allocate capital to clients affords us a heck of a lot of runway.

items.text: Morgan Stanley committed to advancing through $10 trillion in total client assets and expanding capabilities through the wealth funnel and global distribution of asset management offerings.
items.quote: We are deploying capital and expanding capabilities through the wealth funnel and enhancing the global distribution of our asset management offerings... We are committed to advancing through $10 trillion in total client assets and onto the next phase of Morgan Stanley's growth trajectory.

items.text: Morgan Stanley formalized an 'integrated firm' organization to scale client opportunities, positioning leadership talent and integrating data, risk management, and infrastructure.
items.quote: we have formalized the integrated firm by positioning leadership talent at the center of client coverage, integrated data, risk management, and infrastructure to drive growth as we serve more clients across their full suite of needs.

items.text: Morgan Stanley's strategic deck describes the integrated firm as delivering unmatched capabilities throughout clients' growth cycles, including 'Founders Wealth Strategies', 'Family Office Solutions, Trust & Estate Planning', and 'Private Shares Trading & Lending' to help founders and employees preserve wealth and unlock liquidity.
items.quote: Founders Wealth Strategies; Preserve Wealth; Family Office Solutions, Trust & Estate Planning; Unlock Liquidity - Private Shares Trading & Lending

items.text: CFO Sharon Yeshaya described capturing IPO-related flows across the full cap table, using the full cap table and understanding of early investors to bring assets into advice-based relationships.
items.quote: we have a full cap table. We understand early investors... an endowment that might receive a stock associated with an IPO... might take that and put it through... into a Morgan Stanley advice-based relationship.

items.text: Morgan Stanley closed the acquisition of EquityZen to enhance its leadership in the private markets ecosystem and deepen market access for clients, and is focused on covering growth companies and their employees from founding to public maturity.
items.quote: We closed the acquisition of EquityZen, enhancing our leadership position in the private credit markets ecosystem... The objective is to cover growth companies and their employees from founding to their public maturity while broadening access for investors to the growing stack of private companies.

items.text: Sharon Yeshaya described an exclusive partnership with Carta to refer private companies and their employees to Morgan Stanley as they transition to going public, creating a seamless experience.
items.quote: we have an exclusive partnership with Carta, which means that they will refer those private different stock plans or different corporate companies to Morgan Stanley as they move into going public.

items.text: Morgan Stanley launched a digital asset pilot through its partnership with Zero Hash, enabling select clients to buy and sell digital currencies through E*TRADE, and is investing in agentic infrastructure.
items.quote: We launched our digital asset pilot through our partnership with Zero Hash, enabling select clients to buy and sell several major digital currencies through E*TRADE, and we are investing in the development of our agentic infrastructure.

items.text: Morgan Stanley emphasized its strategy to introduce and educate retail clients to the value of advice, alongside acquisitions of EquityZen, expanded partnership with Carta, and collaboration with Zero Hash as strategic initiatives for growth.
items.quote: Our intentional strategy to introduce and educate retail clients to the value of advice, coupled with consistent education over the past several years, sets our franchise apart and positions us to continue to outperform.

items.text: Morgan Stanley stated its growth pillar is about smart, strategic investment into wealth, Institutional Securities, and Investment Management, generating new opportunities to capture client share.
items.quote: growth is about smart, strategic investments across the firm, which generate new opportunities to capture client share.

a7.MS.reason: Multiple passages contain leadership statements and strategic initiatives showing commitment to capturing wealth transfer opportunities (integrated firm strategy, $10 trillion client asset goal, EquityZen/Carta/Zero Hash partnerships, founders/family office capabilities).

CEO Paul Shoukry described (transcript, period March 31, 2026) that a financial advisor knows the client's wife and family and financial objectives, emphasizing deep personal relationships with entire families rather than just transactions or portfolio returns.

Paul Shoukry stated (4Q25 transcript, period September 30, 2025) that the Private Wealth Advisor Program offers education, training, and accreditation along with enhanced capabilities and product solutions, enabling advisors to meet the needs of their most sophisticated clients.

Raymond James remains focused (transcript, period June 30, 2025) on providing education, training, accreditation, and enhanced capabilities and product solutions in the private wealth space to allow advisors to meet the needs of their most sophisticated clients.
Raymond James offers private wealth resources through 'Private Wealth to help advisors serve the complex needs of HNW and UHNW families,' as stated in the investor day deck (published June 5, 2025).

Bank of America Private Bank advisors facilitate conversations across generations to align financial plans with family values, helping clients preserve wealth, prepare heirs, and plan for extended lifespans (research, published June 17, 2026).

Merrill executives touted (trade press, published November 16, 2026) that recruited assets to the wealth unit doubled year-over-year as the firm returned to veteran broker recruiting, after Co-Presidents Lindsay Hans and Eric Schimpf restored a focus on hiring and a more aggressive offer. Why it might matter: the return to veteran broker recruiting (after pulling back at end of 2017) signals a renewed push to capture established advisors and their client assets.

Raymond James provides advisors additional resources to support high-net-worth clients, with an advisor citing its advanced technology and private wealth capabilities as resources for the sophisticated needs of high-net-worth clients within a people-first culture (trade press, published November 5, 2026). Why it might matter: the statement positions the firm's technology and private wealth capabilities as resources for attracting and retaining sophisticated clients.

Merrill's Advisor Development Program roles are designed to build a book of high-net-worth clients through acquiring, building and managing client relationships (recruiting web page, content as of November 3, 2026). Why it might matter: the program is the mechanism by which Merrill develops new advisors capable of building high-net-worth client books, underpinning its succession and growth strategy.

claims.text: Schwab's CEO Wurster stated (3Q26 transcript, period September 30, 2026) the retail business is built to win across generations, and that Schwab is well positioned to continue serving future generations when wealth is passed on, with an extremely high retention rate around wealth transfers. Why it might matter: the firm reports roughly 80% of retail assets are held by ultra-high net worth and high net worth households, the wealth most likely to be passed on, so its high retention around transfers is central to its multi-generational franchise.

Schwab states (3Q26 transcript, period September 30, 2026) that building deeper, longer-lasting relationships and retaining trusted relationships into the decades to come is why it is investing in both people and technology, including financial consultants and wealth advisors. Why it might matter: the firm cites that retail clients with a dedicated financial consultant generate about 3x household NNA and 5x managed investing net flows, quantifying the payoff of these relationship investments.

CFO Sharon Yeshaya described (3Q26 transcript, period September 30, 2026) capturing IPO-related flows across the full cap table, using the full cap table and understanding of early investors to bring assets into advice-based relationships. Why it might matter: the firm reported just over half of its Q3 2026 net new assets were associated with IPO-related flows, illustrating the scale of this capture opportunity.

Merrill added about 4,200 net new households with at least $500,000 in assets in 3Q26 (up 17%), demonstrating demand for advice and ability to attract clients and experienced advisers, per CFO Alastair Borthwick (3Q26 transcript, period September 30, 2026). Why it might matter: the firm frames these results as reflecting strong demand for advice and its ability to attract clients and experienced advisers, indicating growth momentum in wealthy households.

Edward Jones states (10-K, period December 31, 2025) its initiatives include targeting new clients: High Net Worth; Workplace; and a new digital platform focused on attracting and retaining Next Generation investors. Why it might matter: the firm's principal Katherine Roy separately stated advisors work with local business owners every day and the firm wants to create opportunities to expand access to retirement plans, reflecting a lifecycle-based pull-through strategy.

Edward Jones principal Katherine Roy stated (trade press, published September 30, 2026) the firm's advisors work with local business owners every day and the firm wants to create opportunities for advisors to expand access to retirement plans, supported by a new AI-powered retirement plan management tool developed with Aboon and Retirement Plan Advisory Group. Why it might matter: the firm currently has about $50 billion in 401(k) assets across about 10 record keepers, and the new tool aims to reach business owners who lack a plan or have a smaller workforce.

Merrill launched new data analytics fees and a basis points revenue share for third-party managers effective January 1, 2027, to give third parties visibility and recommendation from brokers (trade press, published September 29, 2026). Why it might matter: the firm states it will have a financial incentive to make available and recommend products from third-party firms that pay fees for data analytics, shaping its product distribution.

Raymond James positions itself as a 'destination for private wealth advisors and the clients they serve,' with Private Client Group President Tash Elwyn stating the firm is committed to serving individuals and families with significant wealth (trade press, published September 29, 2026). Why it might matter: the firm frames significant-wealth clients as requiring truly personal advice backed by the right resources, positioning its platform for that segment.

Raymond James has built out a private wealth platform including the Private Wealth Advisor designation program (launched September 2022), providing training, coaching and a peer network for advisors specializing in high-net-worth clients (generally at least $5 million in investable assets); nearly 450 advisors had earned the designation as of September 2026 (trade press, published September 29, 2026). Why it might matter: the firm describes the program as a key recruitment and retention signal as it competes for advisors who build practices around affluent households.

Raymond James launched Private Wealth Guided Portfolios, risk-based model portfolios integrating traditional (equity and fixed income) and alternative investments with a dedicated alternatives allocation, for advisors serving high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth clients (trade press, published September 29, 2026). Why it might matter: the launch extends the firm's alternatives capability to a model-portfolio framework, deepening its offering for wealthy families.

Raymond James's broader high-net-worth effort includes estate and charitable planning capabilities, lending and cash management solutions, risk management services, and intergenerational wealth strategies, positioned as tools for advisors serving households with complex profiles (trade press, published September 29, 2026). Why it might matter: 'intergenerational wealth strategies' is an explicit tool for multi-generational planning, central to capturing wealth transfer.

Raymond James agreed to acquire Clark Capital Management Group, a Philadelphia-based asset manager known for advisor-centric model portfolios and a dedicated high-net-worth service team, which closed in April/May 2026 and added Clark Capital as an independent boutique within Raymond James Investment Management (trade press, published September 29, 2026). Why it might matter: the acquisition adds a dedicated high-net-worth service team and advisor-centric model portfolios, strengthening its managed-portfolio infrastructure for wealthy clients.

Merrill launched a Tax Efficient Transition Service (TET) and Dollar Cost Averaging (DCA) Service to help clients implement tax-efficient transitions and systematic cash deployment within personalized investment strategies (press, published September 15, 2026). Why it might matter: the services address the common challenge of transitioning appreciated assets without realizing all the tax impact at once, directly relevant to wealth transfer and asset transition.

Jay Link, Head of Fiduciary Programs and Platforms at Merrill, said (press, published September 15, 2026) the new services help clients stay focused on their long-term financial goals, including transitioning appreciated assets tax-efficiently and investing cash without timing the market. Why it might matter: the services are positioned to help clients address tax impact and market-timing pressure, both relevant to preserving wealth across transitions.

Edward Jones states (trade press, published August 18, 2026) it has taken a minority stake in the personal finance app Quicken, with the intention of integrating Quicken's personal financial management capabilities into Edward Jones to support its value proposition and advisor conversations with clients. Why it might matter: the investment is framed as reinforcing how technology can support deeper conversations with clients, a capability relevant to serving next-generation clients.

Schwab acquired Wealth.com and rolled out AI-powered estate planning tools to clients, enhancing tax, trust and estate capabilities as part of its wealth offer (1Q26 transcript, period March 31, 2026). Why it might matter: the firm is also working to launch Wealth.com's AI-powered tax planning capability in the near future, extending the estate-planning push into tax planning.

Schwab is expanding its branch footprint and hiring hundreds of financial consultants and wealth consultants to deepen relationships with higher net worth retail clients and their families (transcript, period March 31, 2025). Why it might matter: the firm plans about a dozen new branches for 2026 and to keep investing in 2026 and 2027, signaling sustained commitment to advisor-led relationship deepening.

Schwab is enhancing its tax, trust and estate capabilities, including plans to offer wealth.com's estate planning tools to retail clients, as part of its wealth business investments (2Q25 transcript, period June 30, 2025). Why it might matter: the firm later increased its strategic investment in Wealth.com and began rolling out AI-powered estate planning tools, indicating follow-through on this capability build-out.

Morgan Stanley closed the acquisition of EquityZen to enhance its leadership in the private markets ecosystem and deepen market access for clients, and is focused on covering growth companies and their employees from founding to public maturity (1Q26 transcript, period March 31, 2026; 4Q25 transcript, period December 31, 2025). Why it might matter: the acquisition extends Morgan Stanley's reach into the private markets ecosystem, a key source of future wealth and wealth-transfer relationships.

Morgan Stanley launched a digital asset pilot through its partnership with Zero Hash, enabling select clients to buy and sell digital currencies through E*TRADE, and is investing in agentic infrastructure (1Q26 transcript, period March 31, 2026). Why it might matter: the digital asset pilot extends the E*TRADE channel to a younger, digitally-native client base, supporting the firm's top-of-funnel acquisition strategy.

Edward Jones states (10-K, period December 31, 2025) the Partnership is subject to risk from generational wealth transfer, including changing client expectations and demographics, and is making significant investments in financial advisors and other human capital, technology, digital initiatives, and strategic relationships to support long-term growth. Why it might matter: the firm separately attributes net new asset outflows to generational wealth transfers outside the firm, making this risk tangible rather than hypothetical.

Edward Jones states (10-K, period December 31, 2025) the Partnership seeks to address its strategic risks, most notably competition for clients and personnel in light of the generational wealth transfer, through initiatives to deliver enhanced value and impact, and is making significant investments to attract and retain qualified talent. Why it might matter: the firm frames these investments as necessary to compete for both clients and personnel as demographics shift.

Raymond James's private wealth advisor program and expanded alternative investments platform are described by CEO Paul Shoukry as supporting advisors who focus on high-net-worth clients (transcript, period December 31, 2025). Why it might matter: the firm frames these investments as necessary to continue retaining and attracting the best advisors.

Morgan Stanley's strategic deck (published January 15, 2026) describes the integrated firm as delivering unmatched capabilities throughout clients' growth cycles, including Founders Wealth Strategies, Family Office Solutions, Trust & Estate Planning, and Private Shares Trading & Lending to help founders and employees preserve wealth and unlock liquidity. Why it might matter: the deck positions these capabilities as central to serving clients from founding through public maturity and wealth preservation.

Morgan Stanley emphasized (4Q25 transcript, period December 31, 2025) its strategy to introduce and educate retail clients to the value of advice, alongside acquisitions of EquityZen, expanded partnership with Carta, and collaboration with Zero Hash as strategic initiatives for growth. Why it might matter: the firm positions consistent client education as setting its franchise apart and positioning it to continue to outperform.

Merrill continues to invest in recruiting experienced advisors and a training program to improve net new flows, according to CFO Alastair Borthwick (4Q25 transcript, period December 31, 2025). Why it might matter: the firm separately reports about one-third of net new households in Q2 were added by newly trained advisors, demonstrating the training program's contribution to growth.

claims.text: An executive who consults with HNW-focused advisors on family governance planning states (Cerulli, published October 29, 2025) that advisors must see the client as the entire family and are being equipped to serve the whole family. Why it might matter: Cerulli frames the transfer of wealth as one of the greatest demographic shifts of the 21st century, elevating the importance of whole-family service.

Cerulli states (published October 29, 2025) that firms best prepared to meet recipients' needs are likely to shift marketshare. Why it might matter: Cerulli projects households will transfer $123.7 trillion by 2048, so capturing even a portion of recipients' preferences can shift meaningful marketshare.

claims.text: In response to growing demand for private investment product alternatives for ultra-high-net-worth clients, Raymond James further developed its private capital raising expertise and brought in bespoke private investment alternatives in fiscal 2025 (3Q25 transcript, period September 30, 2025). Why it might matter: the firm was also recognized as the most trusted company among advised investors in wealth management in the J.D. Power 2025 U.S. Investor Satisfaction Study, reinforcing its position with wealthy clients.

Morgan Stanley committed (3Q25 transcript, period September 30, 2025) to advancing through $10 trillion in total client assets and expanding capabilities through the wealth funnel and global distribution of asset management offerings. Why it might matter: the $10 trillion client-asset goal is a stated growth milestone, indicating the firm's forward ambition for capturing assets.

Chairman and CEO Ted Pick stated (2Q25 transcript, period June 30, 2025) the firm is focused on the core strategy of raise, manage, and allocate capital and on nurturing existing businesses, with acquisitions evaluated only if they fit the strategy and offer incremental operating leverage. Why it might matter: the firm frames this core strategy as affording 'a heck of a lot of runway,' signaling durable organic growth capacity.

Schwab's CEO stated (transcript, period March 31, 2025) it will open branches to capture the migration of wealth and reposition some branches, and expects to grow roughly 250 new financial and wealth consultants during 2025, continuing in 2026 and 2027. Why it might matter: the branch expansion is explicitly tied to the migration of wealth across the country, a geographic dimension of wealth transfer the firm is targeting.

Morgan Stanley articulated a strategy to 'raise, manage, and allocate capital' for clients and described its four pillars of the integrated firm (strategy, culture, financial strength, growth) as central to capturing client share (4Q24 transcript, period December 31, 2024). Why it might matter: the firm frames the integrated-firm thesis as the basis for generating new opportunities to capture client share, positioning it for growth across wealth, Institutional Securities, and Investment Management.

Morgan Stanley formalized an 'integrated firm' organization (4Q24 transcript, period December 31, 2024) to scale client opportunities, positioning leadership talent and integrating data, risk management, and infrastructure. Why it might matter: the reorganization is positioned to drive growth by serving more clients across their full suite of needs.

Sharon Yeshaya described (4Q24 transcript, period December 31, 2024) an exclusive partnership with Carta to refer private companies and their employees to Morgan Stanley as they transition to going public. Why it might matter: the partnership gives Morgan Stanley an early and exclusive channel into private companies and their employees before they become public-company wealth holders.

Morgan Stanley stated (4Q24 transcript, period December 31, 2024) its growth pillar is about smart, strategic investment into wealth, Institutional Securities, and Investment Management, generating new opportunities to capture client share. Why it might matter: the growth pillar is explicitly framed as generating opportunities to capture client share, tying strategic investment directly to asset and relationship capture.

Schwab states (3Q26 transcript, period September 30, 2026) approximately 70% of new-to-firm retail households are Gen Z and millennials, and is well positioned to serve future generations when wealth is passed on.

Schwab took an ownership stake in Wealth.com and began rolling out its estate analysis capability, giving more tools to help clients integrate estate planning into their investment life (4Q25 transcript, period December 31, 2025).

Raymond James states (10-K, period September 30, 2025) it seeks to mitigate risks of retiring financial advisors without a successor through financial advisor succession planning and broad services and resources to support their practices.
Raymond James offers Succession Planning and Acquisition resources for independent RIAs, including a team of specialists to guide them (web page, content as of July 12, 2026).
