claims.text: Raymond James has a 'Next gen advisor strategy' as part of its recruiting initiatives (investor day deck, published June 5, 2025).

Raymond James states (10-K, period September 30, 2025) individuals who want to become financial advisors can gain experience through the Wealth Management Associate Program or move to the Advisor Mastery Program; it also has a succession planning process for roles within two levels of the Executive Leadership Team.

Raymond James observed (10-K, period September 30, 2025) a competitive recruiting environment amid a trend of advisors departing traditional firms and retiring without an affiliated successor, selling practices to unaffiliated third parties.

The comparison (which firm appears most prepared for the generational wealth transfer and why) cannot be validly made on this evidence: the firms disclose wealth-transfer readiness on different bases and scopes rather than on a common measure. Schwab publishes a wealth-transfer retention rate (~75% of assets retained in a wealth transfer event) and next-generation demographic figures, Raymond James discloses intergenerational wealth strategies and advisor succession figures, Merrill and Edward Jones disclose related preparation initiatives rather than a transfer-specific readiness metric, and Morgan Stanley does not state a wealth-transfer readiness figure in these documents. Because these are different definitions, units, and scopes (and the sources do not rank firms against each other), no single firm can be identified as most prepared on this evidence.

Schwab states (3Q26 transcript, period September 30, 2026) that approximately 70% of new-to-firm retail households are Gen Z and millennials.

Edward Jones cites (10-Q, period September 26, 2025) an aging client base and generational wealth transfers outside the firm, along with macroeconomic volatility, inflationary pressures and shifts in consumer spending, as factors in elevated asset outflows.
Schwab states (4Q25 transcript, period December 31, 2025) it took an ownership stake in Wealth.com and began rolling out their estate analysis capability to its specialists.

Edward Jones states (10-K, period December 31, 2025) it is subject to risk from generational wealth transfer, including changing client expectations for expanded product offerings and technology needs, and changing client demographics, preferences and values.

Edward Jones states (10-K, period December 31, 2025) it addresses strategic risks including generational wealth transfer through initiatives to deliver enhanced value, while making significant investments to attract and retain qualified talent.
Cerulli (published October 29, 2025) advises that advisors must see the client as the entire family and be equipped to serve the whole family.

Merrill continues to add financial advisors to the sales force through its extensive training program and experienced hiring of advisors (2Q25 transcript, period June 30, 2025, Merrill and Private Bank).
Trade press reports (published November 16, 2026) Merrill returned to veteran broker recruiting after pulling back at end of 2017, and recruited assets doubled year-over-year.

Raymond James states (10-K, period September 30, 2025) it seeks to mitigate the risks of departing/retiring financial advisors through financial advisor succession planning and by providing advisors with a broad range of services and resources to support their practices.

Raymond James states (10-K, period September 30, 2025) it conducts ongoing and robust succession planning for roles within two levels of its Executive Leadership Team, reviewed with executive leadership and the Board several times per year.

Morgan Stanley states (4Q25 transcript, period December 31, 2025) it invests to broaden financial advisor capabilities including alternatives and privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office and OCIO, and tailored lending.
Edward Jones is pursuing a new digital platform focused on attracting and retaining Next Generation investors, as one of its initiatives (10-K, period December 31, 2025).

Raymond James' Private Wealth Advisor Program offers education, training, and accreditation along with enhanced capabilities and product solutions to enable advisors to meet the needs of their most sophisticated clients (4Q25 transcript, period September 30, 2025).
Raymond James' private wealth advisor program and expanded alternative investments platform support advisors who focus on high-net-worth clients (transcript, period December 31, 2025).

Raymond James brought in bespoke private investment alternatives for ultra-high net worth clients in response to growing demand for private investment product alternatives (3Q25 transcript, period September 30, 2025).

Raymond James' Private Wealth Advisor designation program (launched September 2022) provides training, coaching, and a peer network for advisors who specialize in high-net-worth clients (generally at least $5 million in investable assets); nearly 450 advisors had earned the designation as of September 2026 (trade press, published September 29, 2026).

Raymond James' high-net-worth effort includes estate and charitable planning capabilities, lending and cash management solutions, risk management services, and intergenerational wealth strategies, positioned as tools advisors can draw on when serving households with complex financial profiles (trade press, published September 29, 2026).

Schwab took an ownership stake in Wealth.com and rolled out its estate analysis capability, giving more tools to help clients integrate estate planning into their investment life (4Q25 transcript, period December 31, 2025).

Raymond James' Private Client Group offers estate and charitable planning capabilities, lending and cash management solutions, risk management services, and intergenerational wealth strategies, positioned as tools advisors can draw on when serving households with complex financial profiles (trade press, published September 29, 2026).

Client assets per advisor cannot be validly compared side by side across the five firms on this evidence. The advisor headcounts use different definitions (Morgan Stanley counts Wealth Management representatives, latest 15,950 at December 31, 2020; Schwab discloses no advisor headcount, only RIA-related employee counts; Edward Jones counts 'financial advisors (actual)' on both whole-firm and U.S. bases; Merrill reports 'total wealth advisors' across all wealth management businesses in GWIM and Consumer Banking; Raymond James counts employee and independent-contractor financial advisors and excludes RCS-division advisors), the client-asset measures differ (Morgan Stanley sums Wealth Management and Investment Management client assets; Schwab's total client assets are assets in custody; Edward Jones reports assets under care; Merrill reports GWIM or Merrill Wealth Management AUM; Raymond James reports assets under administration), and no firm discloses a client-assets-per-advisor figure (the per-advisor ratio is not in the metric definitions file, so it is unverified).
